dependencies.basis: GASTAT Methodology and Quality Report for International Trade in Goods Statistics explicitly states that merchandise export and import statistics are compiled and classified according to the Harmonized System (HS 2022) issued by the World Customs Organization.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The statistics of merchandise exports and imports of Saudi Arabia are compiled and classified in accordance with international standards. For classification purposes, these statistics rely on the Harmonized System (HS 2022) issued by the World Customs Organization (WCO), which is a nomenclature for the description and classification of goods that includes subheadings and their numerical codes, as well as sections and chapters.

dependencies.basis: Same GASTAT international trade methodology confirms HS Code as the primary classification for goods in the statistics.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Data for each statistical unit is compiled based on the following variables: Classification: Goods code according to the Harmonized System (HS Code).

dependencies.basis: FCSC foreign trade methodology and supporting emirate-level (SCAD) documentation state that commodities are classified according to the Harmonized System (HS) of the World Customs Organization, with GCC-specific extensions in the Customs Tariff Classification.
dependencies.evidence_quote: التصنيفات النظام المنسق لوصف وترميز السلع H.S : ( عن منظمة الجمارك العاملية WCO ) (عام 1995 ).

dependencies.basis: Abu Dhabi Statistics Centre (SCAD) merchandise trade methodology (which feeds federal FCSC series) explicitly uses the GCC Customs Tariff Classification, an 8-digit classification based on the Harmonized System, and follows IMTS 2010 with the special trade system (GCC).
dependencies.evidence_quote: Merchandise trade data is collected and compiled in the GCC Customs Tariff Classification, an 8-digit level classification based on the Harmonized System (recommended for use used by customs authorities to identify products when assessing duties and taxes and for gathering statistics).

dependencies.basis: SCAD merchandise trade methodology states use of the special trade system (GCC) as outlined in IMTS 2010, and compilation under the GCC Customs Tariff Classification that implements the GCC Customs Union framework.
dependencies.evidence_quote: SCAD generally follows internationally recognized standards and concepts for compiling and publishing this data, using the special trade system (GCC) as outline in International Merchandise Trade Statistics (IMTS 2010) published by the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs.

dependencies.basis: GASTAT International Trade in Goods Statistics methodology notes that the series is aligned with national accounts frameworks and that trade data flows as accurate inputs within macroeconomic variables; customs data support measurement of imports and exports in the GDP comprehensive revision.
dependencies.evidence_quote: International Trade in Goods Statistics is aligned with the frameworks of the national accounts and the balance of payments. This consistency is achieved through the harmonization of the concepts, definitions, and classifications used in recording exports and imports, ensuring that trade data flows as accurate and reliable inputs within macroeconomic variables.

dependencies.basis: GASTAT comprehensive revision methodology for GDP and national accounts lists the Harmonized System of Foreign Trade Classification (HS) among the main classifications used.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Several statistical classifications have been used as follows: ... 5. Harmonized System of Foreign Trade Classification (HS)

dependencies.basis: FCSC national accounts methodology lists HS (Harmonized System of Foreign Trade) among the classifications applied in the compilation of national accounts.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The main classifications relied upon in national accounts statistics include the following: ... HS (Harmonized System of Foreign Trade)
